authors: Allen, M.J., Owen, H.J.F., Grieve, S.W.D. & Lines, E.R.
title: Manual labelling artificially inflates deep learning-based segmentation performance on RGB images of closed canopy: validation using TLS
relevance: Validates crown segmentation against terrestrial laser scanning instead of hand-drawn labels and finds performance collapses: AP50 falls from 0.670 against manual labels to 0.094 against TLS in Mediterranean forest, 0.142 in boreal, and at IoU 0.75 the maximum AP is 0.051. The mechanism is our recurring one - human RGB labels and model predictions share the same systematic errors, so scoring against them measures agreement rather than accuracy (see ID 163). This bears directly on annotation-plan item 1, the 1-3k hand-drawn 2020 crowns: those labels will inflate measured INSTANCE performance, and the collapse is concentrated in LOCALIZATION, which is exactly the geometric-versus-thematic split of Q41. Caveat: closed-canopy forest, whereas much of Edmonds is open-grown suburban crowns that are far easier to delineate, so the magnitude will not transfer even though the mechanism does.

authors: Huang, C., Ding, Y., Xiao, K., Liu, R. & Sun, Y.
title: Ladder-side-tuning of visual foundation model for city-scale individual tree detection from high-resolution remote sensing images
relevance: Tree-SAM: city-scale individual tree detection built on SAM with ladder-side-tuning, reporting F1 0.830 and AP@50 0.526 in the URBAN scenario against 0.762/0.478 in forest - notably better in cities, which is our setting. Ladder-side-tuning matters practically because it adapts a foundation model without backpropagating through it, which is the difference between feasible and infeasible on our Colab budget. This is the current peer-reviewed reference point for the fine-resolution instance stream, which has had no update since Phase 1A. Note the accompanying finding from this search that SAM used OUT OF THE BOX does not beat a custom Mask R-CNN even with good prompts - adaptation is doing the work, not the foundation model.
